content: The following references are presented in a clear and professional manner, suitable for a medical expert: 1. The study titled Association between disturbed sleep and depression in children and youths: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies was published in JAMA Network Open in 2021 (Volume 4, e212373-e). It explores the relationship between sleep disturbances and depressive symptoms in young populations. 2. Bruce ES, Lunt L, and McDonagh JE authored a paper on Sleep in adolescents and young adults, which was published in Clinical Medicine in 2017 (Volume 17, Page 424). This work examines the sleep patterns and challenges faced by adolescents and young adults. 3. Marino C, Andrade B, Montplaisir J, Petit D, Touchette E, Paradis H, et al., conducted a study testing bidirectional, longitudinal associations between disturbed sleep and depressive symptoms in children and adolescents using cross-lagged models. This research was published in JAMA Network Open in 2022 (Volume 5, e2227119). 4. Gee B, Orchard F, Clarke E, Joy A, Clarke T, and Reynolds S performed a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate the effect of non-pharmacological sleep interventions on depression symptoms. Their findings were published in Sleep Medicine Reviews in 2019 (Volume 43, Pages 118-128). 5. Newby H, Hagell A, Marsh AD, and Guthold R discussed opportunities to advance the measurement of adolescent well-being, building on a new conceptual framework. This work was published in BMJ in 2022 (Volume 379). 6. The World Health Organization (WHO) provides a webpage titled Spotlight on adolescent health and well-being, which was accessed on September 10, 2022. It highlights key aspects of adolescent health. 7. The WHO also offers resources on promoting adolescent well-being, accessible via their website as of January 30, 2023. 8. The WHO fact sheet on drowning, accessed on May 6, 2023, provides critical information on the global burden and prevention strategies for drowning incidents. 9. Similarly, the WHO fact sheet on burns, accessed on May 6, 2023, outlines the prevalence, risk factors, and prevention measures for burn injuries. 10. Krug EG, Mercy JA, Dahlberg LL, and Zwi AB authored The world report on violence and health, published in The Lancet in 2002 (Volume 360, Pages 1083-1088). This report examines the global impact of violence on health. 11. The WHO webpage on violence against children, accessed on May 6, 2023, provides detailed insights into the prevalence and prevention of violence targeting children. 12. Stoltenborgh M, Bakermans-Kranenburg MJ, Alink LR, and Van Ijzendoorn MH conducted a meta-analysis on the universality of childhood emotional abuse, published in the Journal of Aggression, Maltreatment & Trauma in 2012 (Volume 21, Pages 870-890). 13. Stoltenborgh M, Bakermans-Kranenburg MJ, and Van Ijzendoorn MH also reviewed the prevalence of child neglect in a meta-analytic study published in Social Psychiatry and Psychiatric Epidemiology in 2013 (Volume 48, Pages 345-355). 14. Moody G, Cannings-John R, Hood K, Kemp A, and Robling M systematically reviewed the international prevalence of self-reported child maltreatment by type and gender. Their findings were published in BMC Public Health in 2018 (Volume 18, Pages 1-15). 15. Sardinha L, Maheu-Giroux M, Stöckl H, Meyer SR, and García-Moreno C provided global, regional, and national prevalence estimates of physical or sexual intimate partner violence against women in 2018. This study was published in The Lancet in 2022 (Volume 399, Pages 803-813). 16. Brent D and Maalouf F contributed a chapter on depressive disorders in childhood and adolescence in Rutter’s Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, edited by Thapar A, Pine DS, Leckman JF, Scott S, Snowling MJ, and Taylor E, published by Wiley-Blackwell in 2015. 17. Ogundipe O, Amoo E, Adeloye D, and Olawole-Isaac A conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on substance use among adolescents in sub-Saharan Africa, published in the South African Journal of Child Health in 2018. 18. Mehra VM, Keethakumar A, Bohr YM, Abdullah P, and Tamim H examined the association between alcohol, marijuana, illegal drug use, and e-cigarette use among youth in Canada. Their study was published in BMC Public Health in 2019 (Volume 19, Pages 1-10). 19. Lees B, Meredith LR, Kirkland AE, Bryant BE, and Squeglia LM reviewed the effects of alcohol use on the adolescent brain and behavior, published in Pharmacology Biochemistry and Behavior in 2020 (Volume 192, Article 172906). 20. Salmansadeh H, Ahmadi-Soleimani SM, Pachenari N, Azadi M, Halliwell RF, Rubino T, et al., reviewed evidence on the long-term effects of adolescent drug exposure on brain development and behavior.
